clue.text: Basic equipment needed for standard home exchange

parts.note: stock means standard or usual, as in a stock reply
in means at home
trade means exchange, as in swapping goods

explanation.surface: Equipment for swapping houses is described as a basic necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: The tools and goods a business always keeps on hand are its basic kit, a fixed idiom for essential resources.

clue.text: Rear gunner's final two are more serious

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

indicators.note: the last pair of letters of the word gunner's are taken

explanation.surface: A tail gunner's last two missions turn out to be graver ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, meaning grimmer or graver.

clue.text: Obscure quality of work on a centre of population

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a city is a large centre of population

explanation.surface: A study of some dark aspect of labour in a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the property of being murky or hard to see through or understand.

clue.text: Cut-price floor

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement storey.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockdown price is a heavily reduced one, and to floor someone is to fell them with a blow.

clue.text: Requirements from northern river flowing north to south

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word flowing north is read upwards, so river runs backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and on the English-Welsh border

explanation.surface: Water supplies taken from a northern river that runs from north to south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing north' turns DEE into EED, read up the column; 'to south' then adds S below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things required, so the two plurals are synonyms.

clue.text: Newly-developed porcelain lacking no imitation

indicators.note: something newly developed has been made over, so these letters are rearranged
lacking says the letters that follow are taken out of porcelain

explanation.surface: A fresh type of china that lacks nothing is passed off as a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes N and O from PORCELAIN, leaving PRCELAI, which 'Newly-developed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, an imitation of an original.

clue.text: University administrator accepts notice quietly and without expression

indicators.note: a dean who accepts something takes it inside, so the other letters go into the word

parts.note: a dean is a senior university administrator
an ad is a notice in a newspaper
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A college official takes a notice silently and with a blank face.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no feeling, the stony look of a comic delivering a joke straight.

clue.text: Cuts the leftover lamb joints

explanation.surface: Slicing up what remains of the Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the brush-off is to snub or ignore them, and cooked shoulders of lamb served cold the next day are leftovers.

clue.text: Manage to insert topic on reflection

indicators.note: to manage letters is to handle and arrange them, so these are reordered

explanation.surface: Trying to slip a subject into a discussion after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link into 'on reflection', but it is part of the fodder; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Introspection is looking inward at one's own thoughts, a kind of self-examining thought.

clue.text: Cooking range covered in eggs and herb

indicators.note: something covered in eggs has eggs around it, so the egg letters wrap the rest

parts.note: O looks like an egg, so two eggs are two Os

indicators.note: cooking is a common signal that letters are being stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove smeared with egg, alongside some seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking range' reads as a stove, but 'Cooking' is the signal to rearrange 'range', and the shuffled letters sit between the two egg-shaped Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic plant related to marjoram, used as a seasoning in Italian food.

clue.text: Give reasons why former student is in agony

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the student letter is in the word for agony, so it sits inside it

parts.note: pain is agony
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Justifying why an old pupil is suffering badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to account for something, making it clear by giving the causes.

clue.text: Place abandoned by brown in front of Scottish church

indicators.note: one piece is placed in front of the other, so the colour comes first

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
kirk is the Scottish word for church

explanation.surface: A brown building stands before a Scottish church in a place left deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: The French port was abandoned in the 1940 evacuation of British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel port was famously evacuated by the British army in 1940, so it is a place left behind.

clue.text: One in charge of catching herring on Sunday?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a kipper is a split, smoked herring

explanation.surface: A trawler captain hauls in herring even on the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a boat or team, the person in command.

clue.text: Tough dry grass covering the borders of Richmond

indicators.note: the hay covers the other letters by wrapping round them

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Coarse dried grass lines the edges of a Richmond lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy plant or person is robust and able to survive harsh conditions.

clue.text: An artist may use them in a spoilt sort of way

indicators.note: the letters are put into a different sort of arrangement

explanation.surface: Some painters work in a deliberately spoiled manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Paints made with linseed are a classic medium for a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Show disappearing skill and fail to make contact

explanation.surface: A performer whose talent has gone also drops out of touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's touch is to forfeit a knack, and to stop communicating with someone is to drift apart.

clue.text: Objectively, we admit forcing open rebellions

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: us is the objective case of we
prising means levering or forcing open

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to breaking in during a series of revolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' signals the grammatical object form of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisings are revolts in which people rise up against authority.

clue.text: Rejection of mainly rubbish — half of meal!

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: refuse is rubbish or waste

indicators.note: half of the word meal is taken, here its second two letters

explanation.surface: Turning down most of the scraps, plus half a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, the act of turning something down.

clue.text: Red television socket that covers core of flex

indicators.note: the socket covers the other letters by holding them inside

parts.note: a SCART is the European 21-pin socket for connecting a TV to other equipment

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A crimson TV plug wrapped round the inner wire of a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCART socket was the standard audio-video connector on European televisions; 'core of flex' gives its middle letters, LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of the colour, as in a scarlet uniform.

clue.text: Guests start to wander into the trees

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: Visitors begin to stroll off into the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small wood or group of trees.

clue.text: A spent force in the Netherlands?

definitions.text: A spent force in the Netherlands?

parts.words: A spent force in the Netherlands?
parts.note: a spent force normally means something past its best, but here it is money once spent in Holland, a currency replaced by the euro

explanation.surface: Something in Holland that has lost its power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch currency was withdrawn in 2002, so it is now an old coin no longer spent.

clue.text: Notice rising odour and answer

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word for odour runs backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
to answer can mean to serve, as in that will answer the purpose

explanation.surface: Spotting a smell that comes up and responding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BO into OB in the down column.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to see or perceive, a synonym for to notice.

clue.text: Had some food on the way back — delayed because of puncture!

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: fed means had a meal
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Someone ate on the return journey and was late because of a flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns FED into DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctured tyre goes flat as the air escapes, which is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Strange — that's always in front!

indicators.note: always is placed in front of the other piece

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something odd always pushes to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic form of ever; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, uncanny in a way that causes unease.

clue.text: Match fixed — what to wear?

parts.note: to twin is to pair or match
set means fixed, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A rigged game, then a question about clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together, a classic women's outfit.

clue.text: He governs over the way one does stocktaking

indicators.note: the ruler sits over the way, holding it inside

parts.note: someone who governs is a ruler
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A governor who oversees an inventory check in his shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here means livestock and taking means stealing, so this is a cattle thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a cattle thief, someone who steals livestock.

clue.text: Eye opener in ground breaking experience

indicators.note: the eye's opening letter goes in the rearranged letters
breaking ground smashes it up, so its letters are rearranged
an opener is a word's first letter

explanation.surface: A revelation made during a pioneering trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges GROUND to UNDRGO, and 'in' places the E from 'Eye opener' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through it, to live through an experience.

clue.text: Develop — or these lochs will get drier

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecast that Scottish lakes will dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' looks like the comparative adjective, but it is a noun: something that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame airs washing on rails, a device for drying laundry indoors.
